page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL processor cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz, the CPU includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AES. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and includes 154 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with Premium Storage capability.

Benchmark data indicates that the D4ds_v4 delivers modest performance across compute and memory subsystems. In stress-ng and PassMark CPU evaluations, both single-core and multi-core performance fall within the bottom 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks, including read and write operations on large uncached blocks, also place in the lower quartile, though PassMark memory scores and single-threaded gzip compression achieve average tier results. Cryptographic and vector instruction capabilities are present, but database operations such as Redis SET and static web serving throughput remain in the lower performance tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4ds_v4 offers a balanced resource density for workloads requiring a mix of compute, memory, and local storage without demanding high-performance hardware. The inclusion of local storage and Premium Storage capability makes it suitable for lightweight databases, development environments, and general-purpose application hosting. However, for compute-intensive tasks, large-scale data processing, or high-throughput web serving, the performance tradeoffs observed in multi-threaded benchmarks suggest that alternative compute-optimized or higher-tier instances may be required.
